name: Space Shuttle Challenger
best_known_for: OV-099 — second operational Shuttle. Lost 73 seconds after launch on STS-51-L (1986-01-28) with all seven crew, including teacher Christa McAuliffe
credit: Built from a structural test article (STA-099) converted to flight configuration when Enterprise was deemed too expensive to upgrade. First flight STS-6 (1983-04-04) — the first Shuttle EVA. Flew 10 missions before being lost. STS-51-L (1986-01-28) launched at unprecedented cold (−1 °C), causing the right SRB's O-rings to fail seal; hot gas burned through the strut attaching the SRB to the external tank, the tank ruptured, and the orbiter broke apart at Max-Q (T+73s) at 14 km altitude. The crew compartment fell intact and impacted the Atlantic ~2:45 later; all seven crew (Smith, Scobee, Resnik, McNair, Onizuka, Jarvis, McAuliffe) perished. The Rogers Commission ground the Shuttle for 32 months and rewrote NASA's safety culture — every subsequent program design dates to lessons learned here.
